name: Shillong
description: Capital city and district headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Scenic hill station at about 1,496 m elevation with colonial charm, pine forests, lakes, waterfalls, and as the cultural and educational hub of the Northeast.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills and capital of Meghalaya
Average elevation around 1496 metres
About 100 km from Guwahati airport/rail
Known for educational institutions and music scene

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, about 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and on clear days toward the Bangladesh plains. Sacred to the Khasi as the abode of U Lei Shillong.
facts: Highest peak in the state at ~1965 m
About 10 km from Shillong city centre
Sacred site for Khasi deity U Lei Shillong
Popular for sunrise and sunset views

name: Elephant Falls
description: Multi-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, about 12 km from the city centre. Known locally as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew (three-step waterfall). Named after a rock resembling an elephant that was destroyed in the 1897 earthquake.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city
Three-step cascade amid ferns and greenery
Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall
Easily accessible with paved paths and stairs

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial lake in the heart of Shillong, named after Sir William Ward. Features gravel paths, flower gardens, boating facilities, and is a popular spot for walks and relaxation amid the city.
facts: Also known locally as Nan Polok
Named after former Chief Commissioner of Assam
Located in central Shillong
Popular for morning walks and boating

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum and research centre in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artefacts, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across multiple galleries. A key educational and tourist destination.
facts: Located in Mawlai, Shillong
Nineteen galleries on Northeast indigenous cultures
Research library and conference facilities
Popular with students and tourists

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Sub-divisional town on the southern plateau of East Khasi Hills, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Famous for waterfalls, living root bridges, caves, and dramatic views over the Bangladesh plains. Local name Sohra is now preferred.
facts: Average elevation about 1430 metres
Once held world rainfall records
About 54 km south of Shillong
Base for exploring Sohra region's attractions

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 metres, plunging from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Fed by plateau rainwater; named after the tragic Khasi legend of Ka Likai. Spectacular viewpoint near Sohra.
facts: Height approximately 340 metres
Tallest plunge waterfall in India
About 7 km from Sohra town
Named after local legend of Ka Likai

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall dropping about 315 metres over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai, south of Sohra. Also known as Seven Sisters or Mawsmai Falls; most impressive during monsoon when segments span the cliff.
facts: Height about 315 metres
Seven segments during full flow
Near Mawsmai village, about 1 km south
Popular viewpoint overlooking Bangladesh plains

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with electric lighting, stalactites, stalagmites, and some fossils. Short tourist route of about 150 metres; one of the easiest caves to explore in Meghalaya.
facts: About 6 km from Sohra town
Lit tourist section ~150 m long
Formed by dissolution of limestone
Popular easy cave experience

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block known as the cleanest in Asia (Discover India, 2003) and India (2005). Features neat homes, bamboo dustbins, living root bridges nearby, skywalk, and views toward Bangladesh. Matrilineal Khasi community.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003
About 90 km from Shillong near Bangladesh border
100% literacy reported; matrilineal society
Nearby living root bridge and bamboo skywalk

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica over generations. Requires a steep trek of about 3,000-3,500 steps from Tyrna. Iconic example of Khasi bioengineering.
facts: Located in Nongriat village near Sohra
Trek from Tyrna involves ~3500 steps down
Estimated over 180 years old for lower bridge
Only double-decker of its kind

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic viewpoint and canyon about 25 km from Shillong, meaning 'end of the hills' in Khasi. Offers expansive views of layered green hills, valleys, and distant plains. Popular for photography and short treks.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong, near Smit
Elevation around 1600 m
Name means end of the hills or slopes
Free entry; best in clear weather

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village, about 25 km from Shillong. Protected for centuries by Khasi tradition; no removal of anything from the forest. Rich biodiversity, monoliths, and cultural significance.
facts: About 25 km southwest of Shillong
One of the most famous law-kyntang sacred groves
Visitors must not remove anything from the forest
Home to old trees, orchids, and cultural sites
